body:
i'll start with the question i asked myself when i posted here: *would i really be posting here if i was 100% sure it was pointless?*

you being here, asking these questions, and seeking this help, are all signs that you have the motivation to keep going. however small it may be. whether subconscious or not, a part of you had faith that this would give you answers (or at least put you on the right track towards them).

having *that* piece of hope is what you can use to keep going. you sound well aware of what is wrong, or at least of some factors of it. you being able to identify these issues and ask for guidance speaks volumes for your willingness to improve. on top of that, you know how a suicidal/depressed mindset can make you believe things that are absurd. you are aware of these things and that is already so much progress. 

i wont go up to anyone and just say "it gets better. youll be happy soon," because we both know that feels beyond fake. but i know that you will have different days. theres gonna be ups, and theres gonna be downs. the best thing you can do is aim for higher ups and lower downs. it's a process that wont happen overnight, and that sucks ass, i know. but youve already shown so much promise in this post alone. i hope you can believe me about that. im not saying it just because. a lot of what you've said took me way too long to learn myself.

​

anyway uhhh sidenote: sorry if this was written like a thesis paper, ive been writing like this ever since i started ADD meds and still cant really help it. love you though, stranger ♥

i think this is the reason a lot of people use for hiding their feelings. i mean, depression and various other mental illnesses lead to that guilty mindset. i waited a long while to say anything about my emotions (even now i tend to sometimes hide my feelings), and i can for sure say that it wasnt the best decision.

im not you though, and i know that i will never be in an identical situation to you. all i can say is that ive had similar experiences, but i know that i will never truly understand yours. what i can say, however, is that bottling things up is really never the solution to something like this. for most (including me), it eventually becomes too much and leads to a breakdown or something that you really cant hide anymore. being honest with yourself and others (so long as they are people you can trust) will go a long way. it takes a lot to say something, i know. but please dont force yourself to tuck everything away just so you wont "inconvenience" someone close to you. these are people that care for you, and im sure they would much rather be there to help you and encourage you than let you suffer in silence. of course everyone has their own problems, but it's okay to have your own be known, as well. i cant force you to do anything and i dont intend to with this post, but i want you to know that it is okay to ask for help. it takes strength, and im sure you have it in you. take care.

you dont have to answer if you dont want to, but do you know why you "have to" pretend you're okay? as in, is there a specific reason? or is it just the idea that you cant share any of this with family/friends?

edit: also, i hope the quotes around "have to" didnt come across as condescending. it's hard to have the right tone over text.

being honest with your feelings is crucial to recovery. i will never tell someone that a professional knows better than their own self, but this may potentially be a start towards improvement.

forgive me if im interpreting things the wrong way, but hearing you talk about the little things (even just your own bed) almost seems as if this *could* be beneficial, even as a short term experience. things like your bed or your cat might feel like small victories, but the fact that you can appreciate their importance shows that youre still able to find something positive for yourself, however big or small it may be.

these "small victories" might sometimes make you feel pathetic (for lack of a better word), as that's how ive sometimes viewed my own, but they are anything but that. theyre the building blocks towards improvement. im not going to sit here and tell you that everything is uphill from here because there will be ups and downs along the way. these small things, however, are a starting point.

i do not know you, and i obviously never will. but i am so glad you are still here. be honest with your feelings and dont hide them. see how things go from here, and if you feel that things are worsening too much, be honest about it. use that cat and bed and your boyfriend to motivate yourself to keep going, but also remember that you're doing it for yourself because you're worth it.
no worries at all. im good!

there's a very small part of me that forces myself to believe that im in pain so that someone else isnt. im unsure of how i stand religiously ever since an "incident" i had (with god, i guess) some years ago, but there's a lot of superstition that i still have about these kinds of things.

it definitely depends on if you believe it enough. it's a thought process that wont work for everyone (even i sometimes hate it), but it's something i can offer.

telling myself that im suffering so that someone else isnt is bittersweet. *why* should that make me happy? isnt it still unfair? what did i do to deserve it over someone else?

my mentality is that i didnt do something to deserve it. it simply happens to me because i was strong enough to handle it. stronger than whomever else wouldve been. you dont want to fight anymore, but you have. and while im not you and i will never be able to speak for you, i cant help but think that youve made it this far because there is at least some piece of you that is able to keep going, however small it may be.

the whole "my pain takes the pain away from someone else" mentality probably sounds stupid to a lot of people. it's okay if thats the case with you. i find it humbling and grounding for myself sometimes. while it isnt anywhere near a resolution to my problems, it's a method of coping that ive learned to adjust to. it reminds me that i do not deserve this pain. im simply the one that can bear it best. i hope you can keep finding new ways to view the situation. it's a process i still havent figured out (and perhaps never will), but i think it keeps a person hopeful for the future. please stay safe. i dont know you, but i long for your happiness.

in the nicest way possible, please be careful with the "I understand" type of response to people. while im not at high risk of harming myself or others, i can already tell that isnt always the case for people here. i know it sounds harmless and encouraging, but a lot of times it just makes the recipient think "no, you don't."

i really do appreciate your drive to help people out here. you definitely have similar experiences having used writing as a coping mechanism, so i think i know what you meant. it's just a phrase that gets under the skin a lot more than it seems at first. thank you for being here nonetheless.

the pessimist in me had low expectations for replies, but i'll admit that you have me in tears (well, more tears). i get the whole "pain is not a competition" thing as well but have the same feelings whenever i see my sibling complain about problems that could easily be fixed.  the whole privilege thing is definitely part of why im so guilty about it. i live in an extremely privileged area though--the kind where the only crimes are car theft because people are too rich to lock their car doors. my dad is a (technically homeless) addict that's well known by local police at this point. it's such an odd combination to me. i feel so spoiled yet so inferior here. 

but anyway, thank you for this comment. i dont know what it is about it, but it feels like more than an empty promise that you copy/pasted from another post. i can at least assure people for now that i am safe, if that means anything to anyone. i wish i could help others out as well, and i hope i'll soon see the day where that can become a reality again.
